newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures down, seen to drift.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures down, seen to drift.

text.p: Rubber futures drifted lower by midday on Thursday in light trade with the market seen drifting this afternoon in the absence of fresh buying, dealers said.
"It was flat all morning long. It was very quiet and the mood does not look like it will change this afternoon," a local rubber trader said.

Lower Japanese prices further depressed sentiment, dealers said. Tokyo's benchmark February contract slipped 0.8 yen to 139.9 while Kobe's February contract shed 1.2 yen to 139.0 in the first afternoon session.
"It was the same story all over again. Dull and lifeless," another dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, November RSS3 was indicated at 127.50 U.S. cents a kg from 128.50 cents.
November RSS1 was indicated at 183.50-184.50 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.31) a kg from Wednesday's settlement of 184.50 cents.
November TSR20 was indicated at 177.50 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg against the previous 178.50 cents.
